pages.text: Every class has its own kind of home, and each culture has shared buildings too. Their entries give a short $(thing)recipe$(0), not a blueprint: there is no fixed design, only a few rules your build has to satisfy.$(br2)$(thing)Marker block$(0): the block that identifies the structure. Place it inside the build.$(br2)$(thing)Interior$(0): the free space needed inside. Sizes are approximate; build bigger if you like.

$(thing)Floor, Walls, Roof$(0): the materials the build must contain. Where several are listed, include all of them. Woods are listed by the species the culture favours.$(br2)$(thing)Inside$(0): furnishings that must be present, such as a chest, a table or 2+ chairs.$(br2)$(thing)Light$(0): how much of the floor must be lit, and to what level.$(br2)$(thing)Serves$(0): how many citizens can use a shared building at once.

Taller homes list $(thing)storeys$(0) and apply their rules to each one. Fenced plots such as farms need a border of fences and a gate. A $(thing)plaza$(0) or similar compound must sit under the open sky and have other buildings close by.$(br2)Beyond the required blocks you are free to $(thing)decorate$(0). Flourishes never hurt a home, and a lovingly built city is its own reward.
